code.originalText: Six-month heart failure review with repeat echocardiogram

text.paragraph: Six-month heart failure review with repeat echocardiogram. [S]

Mr. Roosevelt returns for his six-month review and repeat echocardiogram. The stomach illness in July settled within four days; he restarted his heart failure medicines on the third day without lightheadedness, and his weight is back to 82 kg. He is finishing an adapted cardiac rehabilitation program of seated arm-cycle and resistance-band training and will keep up the band exercises at home three times a week. He propels his wheelchair on level ground and up short ramps without breathlessness, sleeps on one pillow, and has had no leg swelling since furosemide stopped. His home blood pressures run 115 to 125 systolic, and he has had no lightheadedness on transfers. He has not smoked since April. He prefers not to raise his medicine doses further for now, because safe transfers matter more to him than small further gains, and the July illness showed how quickly his blood pressure can fall. [S]

list.item:
Heart failure with improved ejection fraction (I50.22). Ejection fraction 45 percent today, up from 30 percent in April: heart failure with improved ejection fraction (a rise of at least 10 points to above 40 percent). NYHA class I to II, KCCQ-12 78 (up 40 points), and NT-proBNP 410 pg/mL, down from 2850. Potassium 4.5 mmol/L and creatinine 1.21 mg/dL (eGFR 68), back to baseline after the July illness. Sacubitril/valsartan 49/51 mg and carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily are below target doses; at his request, and given his dependence on safe independent transfers, these are accepted as his tolerated doses for now. [S]
Continue sacubitril/valsartan, carvedilol, spironolactone, and empagliflozin; therapy continues even though the ejection fraction has improved.
No implantable defibrillator: the ejection fraction is above 35 percent.
Revisit dose increases at the three-month review.
